It counts whitespace-separated words, case-insensitively (keys are lowercase).
Keys appear in the order each word is first seen.
reference:
use std.map
use std.str

pub fn word_count(text: Str) -> Map[Str, Int]
  var counts: Map[Str, Int] = {}
  for w in str.words(str.lower(text))
    set counts = map.update(counts, key: w, default: 0, f: fn(n) => n + 1)
  end for
  counts
end fn

    pub fn parse_pairs(text: Str) -> Result[Map[Str, Int], Str]

`text` holds `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, e.g. `"a=1;b=22"`. Surrounding
whitespace around keys and values is ignored; empty segments are skipped.
Return `Err("bad pair: <segment>")` for a segment without exactly one `=`, and
`Err("bad number: <value>")` when the value is not an integer.
reference:
use std.map
use std.str

pub fn parse_pairs(text: Str) -> Result[Map[Str, Int], Str]
  var out: Map[Str, Int] = {}
  for segment in str.split(text, ";")
    if str.trim(segment) == ""
      continue
    end if
    match str.split(segment, "=")
      case [key, value]
        match str.to_int(value)
          case Some(n) => set out = map.put(out, key: str.trim(key), value: n)
          case None => return Err("bad number: ${str.trim(value)}")
        end match
      case _ => return Err("bad pair: ${segment}")
    end match
  end for
  Ok(out)
end fn

  expect solution.parse_pairs(" x = -3 ;; ") == Ok({"x": -3})
  expect solution.parse_pairs("") == Ok({})
end test

test "invalid"
  expect solution.parse_pairs("a=1;b") == Err("bad pair: b")
  expect solution.parse_pairs("a=x") == Err("bad number: x")

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` defining a stack machine:

    pub type Instr
      case Push(value: Int)
      case Add
      case Mul
      case Dup
      case Pop
    end type

    pub fn run(program: List[Instr]) -> Result[List[Int], Str]

The stack starts empty and is returned top-last (the last pushed value is the
last element). `Add`/`Mul` pop two values and push the result; `Dup` pushes a
copy of the top; `Pop` removes the top. Any instruction that needs more values
than are on the stack returns `Err("stack underflow")`.
reference:
use std.list

pub type Instr
  case Push(value: Int)
  case Add
  case Mul
  case Dup
  case Pop
end type

pub fn run(program: List[Instr]) -> Result[List[Int], Str]
  var stack: List[Int] = []
  for instr in program
    set stack = step(stack, instr)?
  end for
  Ok(stack)
end fn

fn step(stack: List[Int], instr: Instr) -> Result[List[Int], Str]
  let n = list.len(stack)
  let rest2 = list.take(stack, n - 2)
  let top2 = list.drop(stack, n - 2)
  match instr
    case Push(v) => Ok(list.push(stack, v))
    case Add | Mul
      match top2
        case [a, b]
          if instr == Add
            Ok(list.push(rest2, a + b))
          else
            Ok(list.push(rest2, a * b))
          end if
        case _ => Err("stack underflow")
      end match
    case Dup
      match stack
        case [.._, top] => Ok(list.push(stack, top))
        case _ => Err("stack underflow")
      end match
    case Pop
      match stack
        case [..rest, _] => Ok(rest)
        case _ => Err("stack underflow")
      end match
  end match
end fn
tests:

test "arithmetic"
  expect solution.run([solution.Push(2), solution.Push(3), solution.Add, solution.Dup, solution.Mul]) == Ok([25])
  expect solution.run([]) == Ok([])
  expect solution.run([solution.Push(1), solution.Push(2), solution.Pop]) == Ok([1])
end test

test "underflow"
  expect solution.run([solution.Add]) == Err("stack underflow")
  expect solution.run([solution.Push(1), solution.Mul]) == Err("stack underflow")
  expect solution.run([solution.Dup]) == Err("stack underflow")
end test

Write `solution.veld` defining:

    pub fn to_roman(n: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]

Convert 1..3999 to Roman numerals (`4 -> "IV"`, `1994 -> "MCMXCIV"`).
Other inputs return `Err("out of range")`.
reference:
use std.list

record Numeral
  value: Int
  symbol: Str
end record

fn numerals() -> List[Numeral]
  [
    Numeral{value: 1000, symbol: "M"},
    Numeral{value: 900, symbol: "CM"},
    Numeral{value: 500, symbol: "D"},
    Numeral{value: 400, symbol: "CD"},
    Numeral{value: 100, symbol: "C"},
    Numeral{value: 90, symbol: "XC"},
    Numeral{value: 50, symbol: "L"},
    Numeral{value: 40, symbol: "XL"},
    Numeral{value: 10, symbol: "X"},
    Numeral{value: 9, symbol: "IX"},
    Numeral{value: 5, symbol: "V"},
    Numeral{value: 4, symbol: "IV"},
    Numeral{value: 1, symbol: "I"},
  ]
end fn

pub fn to_roman(n: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]
  if n < 1 or n > 3999
    return Err("out of range")
  end if
  var rest = n
  var out = ""
  for num in numerals()
    while rest >= num.value
      set out = out + num.symbol
      set rest = rest - num.value
    end while
  end for
  Ok(out)
end fn

  expect solution.to_roman(0) == Err("out of range")
end test

pub fn total(json_text: Str) -> Result[Float, Str]

    case Ok(JArr(items)) => items
    case Ok(_) => return Err("bad item")
    case Err(_) => return Err("invalid json")

  end for
  Ok(sum)

    pub fn search(xs: List[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]

`xs` is sorted ascending with no duplicates. Return the index of `target`
using binary search (O(log n) comparisons), or `None`.
reference:
use std.list

pub fn search(xs: List[Int], target: Int) -> Option[Int]
  var low = 0
  var high = list.len(xs) - 1
  while low <= high
    let mid = (low + high) / 2
    match list.get(xs, mid)
      case Some(v) if v == target => return Some(mid)
      case Some(v) if v < target => set low = mid + 1
      case _ => set high = mid - 1
    end match
  end while
  None
end fn

  expect solution.search(xs, 4) == None

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` defining:

    pub record Item
      sku: Str
      qty: Int
    end record

    pub type Event
      case Received(sku: Str, qty: Int)
      case Shipped(sku: Str, qty: Int)
    end type

    pub fn apply_events(stock: List[Item], events: List[Event]) -> Result[List[Item], Str]

Apply events in order. `Received` adds quantity (creating the item at the end
of the list if new). `Shipped` removes quantity; if the item is missing or
would go negative, return `Err("insufficient <sku>")`. Items keep their order.
reference:
use std.list

pub record Item
  sku: Str
  qty: Int
end record

pub type Event
  case Received(sku: Str, qty: Int)
  case Shipped(sku: Str, qty: Int)
end type

pub fn apply_events(stock: List[Item], events: List[Event]) -> Result[List[Item], Str]
  var items = stock
  for e in events
    set items = match e
      case Received(sku, qty) => adjust(items, sku: sku, delta: qty)
      case Shipped(sku, qty)
        let current = list.find(items, fn(i) => i.sku == sku)
        match current
          case Some(i) if i.qty >= qty => adjust(items, sku: sku, delta: -qty)
          case _ => return Err("insufficient ${sku}")
        end match
    end match
  end for
  Ok(items)
end fn

fn adjust(items: List[Item], sku: Str, delta: Int) -> List[Item]
  if list.any(items, fn(i) => i.sku == sku)
    list.map(items, fn(i) => adjust_one(i, sku: sku, delta: delta))
  else
    list.push(items, Item{sku: sku, qty: delta})
  end if
end fn

fn adjust_one(i: Item, sku: Str, delta: Int) -> Item
  if i.sku == sku
    Item{..i, qty: i.qty + delta}
  else
    i
  end if
end fn

test "events"
  let stock = [solution.Item{sku: "a", qty: 2}]
  let events = [solution.Received(sku: "b", qty: 5), solution.Shipped(sku: "a", qty: 2)]
  expect solution.apply_events(stock, events) == Ok([solution.Item{sku: "a", qty: 0}, solution.Item{sku: "b", qty: 5}])
  expect solution.apply_events(stock, [solution.Shipped(sku: "a", qty: 3)]) == Err("insufficient a")
  expect solution.apply_events([], [solution.Shipped(sku: "z", qty: 1)]) == Err("insufficient z")

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` implementing a turnstile:

    pub type State
      case Locked
      case Unlocked(coins: Int)
      case Broken
    end type

    pub type Event
      case Coin
      case Push
      case Kick
    end type

    pub fn step(state: State, event: Event) -> State
    pub fn run(events: List[Event]) -> State

Rules for `step`:

- `Coin` unlocks a locked turnstile with 1 coin; on an unlocked one it adds a coin.
- `Push` locks an unlocked turnstile again; on a locked one nothing happens.
- `Kick` breaks it, whatever state it is in. A broken turnstile ignores everything.

`run` starts from `Locked` and applies the events in order.
reference:
use std.list

pub type State
  case Locked
  case Unlocked(coins: Int)
  case Broken
end type

pub type Event
  case Coin
  case Push
  case Kick
end type

pub fn step(state: State, event: Event) -> State
  match state, event
    case Broken, _ => Broken
    case _, Kick => Broken
    case Locked, Coin => Unlocked(1)
    case Locked, Push => Locked
    case Unlocked(n), Coin => Unlocked(n + 1)
    case Unlocked(_), Push => Locked
  end match
end fn

pub fn run(events: List[Event]) -> State
  list.fold(events, init: Locked, step: step)
end fn

test "single steps"

  expect solution.step(solution.Unlocked(2), solution.Coin) == solution.Unlocked(3)
  expect solution.step(solution.Unlocked(2), solution.Push) == solution.Locked
  expect solution.step(solution.Locked, solution.Push) == solution.Locked
  expect solution.step(solution.Unlocked(1), solution.Kick) == solution.Broken
  expect solution.step(solution.Broken, solution.Coin) == solution.Broken
end test

test "runs"

  expect solution.run([solution.Coin, solution.Kick, solution.Coin, solution.Push]) == solution.Broken
end test

use std.list
use std.str

pub fn route(method: Str, path: Str) -> Str
  let segments = str.split(path, "/") |> list.filter(fn(s) => s != "")
  match method, segments
    case "GET", [] => "home"
    case "GET", ["users"] => "list users"
    case "POST", ["users"] => "create user"
    case "GET", ["users", id] => "show user ${id}"
    case "DELETE", ["users", id] => "delete user ${id}"
    case _, [] => "405"
    case _, ["users"] => "405"
    case _, ["users", _] => "405"
    case _ => "404"
  end match
end fn

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` with

    pub fn totals(text: Str) -> Result[List[Str], Str]

`text` is CSV with a header line `category,amount` followed by data rows, for
example `food,12`. Sum the amounts per category and return one line per
category, formatted `category: total`, sorted by category name.

- Fields may be quoted (`"office, misc",5`).
- A row that does not have exactly two fields, or whose amount is not an
  integer, makes the whole result `Err("bad row N")`, where N is the line
  number of the row counting the header as line 1.
- A missing or different header is `Err("bad header")`.
- Blank lines are ignored (and do not count as rows).
reference:
use std.csv
use std.list
use std.map
use std.str

pub fn totals(text: Str) -> Result[List[Str], Str]
  let rows = csv.parse(text)?
  match rows
    case [] => Err("bad header")
    case [header, ..data]
      if header != ["category", "amount"]
        return Err("bad header")
      end if
      var sums: Map[Str, Int] = {}
      var line = 1
      for row in data
        set line = line + 1
        match row
          case [category, amount]
            match str.to_int(amount)
              case Some(n) => set sums = map.update(sums, key: category, default: 0, f: fn(total) => total + n)
              case None => return Err("bad row ${line}")
            end match
          case _ => return Err("bad row ${line}")
        end match
      end for
      let names = list.sort(map.keys(sums))
      Ok(list.map(names, fn(name) => "${name}: ${map.get_or(sums, key: name, default: 0)}"))
  end match
end fn

Write `solution.veld` with

    pub fn emails(text: Str) -> List[Str]
    pub fn is_iso_date(text: Str) -> Bool
    pub fn redact_digits(text: Str) -> Str

- `emails` returns every email address in the text, in order. An address is
  letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, then `@`, then a domain of labels made of
  letters, digits and `-`, separated by dots, ending in a dot and at least two
  letters (`bob.smith@mail.example.com`).
- `is_iso_date` is true for exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` with a month 01-12 and a day
  01-31 (it does not need to know month lengths).
- `redact_digits` replaces every run of digits with a single `#`.
reference:
use std.regex

pub fn emails(text: Str) -> List[Str]
  match regex.find_all("""[A-Za-z0-9._-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,}""", text)
    case Ok(found) => found
    case Err(_) => []
  end match
end fn

pub fn is_iso_date(text: Str) -> Bool
  match regex.is_match("""^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$""", text)
    case Ok(ok) => ok
    case Err(_) => false
  end match
end fn

pub fn redact_digits(text: Str) -> Str
  match regex.replace(text, pattern: """\d+""", with: "#")
    case Ok(out) => out
    case Err(_) => text
  end match
end fn

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` implementing a least-recently-used cache of Int values:

    pub record Cache
      capacity: Int
      order: List[Str]          # keys, least recently used first
      values: Map[Str, Int]
    end record

    pub fn new(capacity: Int) -> Cache
    pub fn put(cache: Cache, key: Str, value: Int) -> Cache
    pub fn get(cache: Cache, key: Str) -> Pair[Option[Int], Cache]

`put` inserts or updates a key and makes it the most recently used one. When
that would exceed `capacity`, the least recently used key is evicted first.
`get` returns the value (`None` if absent) together with the cache in which that
key has become the most recently used. A capacity below 1 behaves like 1.
`Pair` is a prelude record with fields `first` and `second`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.map
use std.math

pub record Cache
  capacity: Int
  order: List[Str]
  values: Map[Str, Int]
end record

pub fn new(capacity: Int) -> Cache
  Cache{capacity: math.max(capacity, 1), order: [], values: {}}
end fn

fn touch(order: List[Str], key: Str) -> List[Str]
  list.push(list.filter(order, fn(k) => k != key), key)
end fn

pub fn put(cache: Cache, key: Str, value: Int) -> Cache
  var order = cache.order
  var values = cache.values
  if not map.has(values, key) and list.len(order) >= cache.capacity
    match list.first(order)
      case Some(oldest)
        set order = list.drop(order, 1)
        set values = map.remove(values, oldest)
      case None => set order = order
    end match
  end if
  Cache{..cache, order: touch(order, key), values: map.put(values, key: key, value: value)}
end fn

pub fn get(cache: Cache, key: Str) -> Pair[Option[Int], Cache]
  match map.get(cache.values, key)
    case Some(v) => Pair{first: Some(v), second: Cache{..cache, order: touch(cache.order, key)}}
    case None => Pair{first: None, second: cache}
  end match
end fn

use std.json
use std.list
use std.map
use std.math

record Person
  name: Str
  age: Int
end record

fn person(j: Json) -> Option[Person]
  let name = json.get(j, "name")?
  let age = json.get(j, "age")?

reference:
use std.list

pub fn identity(n: Int) -> List[List[Int]]
  list.map(
    list.range(0, n),
    fn(i)
      list.map(
        list.range(0, n),
        fn(j)
          if i == j
            1
          else
            0
          end if
        end fn,
      )
    end fn,
  )
end fn

fn width(m: List[List[Int]]) -> Int
  match m
    case [] => 0
    case [row, .._] => list.len(row)
  end match
end fn

fn cell(m: List[List[Int]], row: Int, col: Int) -> Int
  match list.get(m, row)
    case Some(r) => list.get(r, col) |> unwrap_int()
    case None => 0
  end match
end fn

fn unwrap_int(o: Option[Int]) -> Int
  match o
    case Some(v) => v
    case None => 0
  end match
end fn

pub fn transpose(m: List[List[Int]]) -> List[List[Int]]
  list.map(list.range(0, width(m)), fn(c) => list.map(m, fn(row) => unwrap_int(list.get(row, c))))
end fn

pub fn multiply(a: List[List[Int]], b: List[List[Int]]) -> Result[List[List[Int]], Str]
  if width(a) != list.len(b)
    return Err("dimension mismatch")
  end if
  let bt = transpose(b)
  Ok(list.map(a, fn(row) => list.map(bt, fn(col) => dot(row, col))))
end fn

fn dot(xs: List[Int], ys: List[Int]) -> Int
  list.sum(
    list.map(list.range(0, list.len(xs)), fn(i) => unwrap_int(list.get(xs, i)) * unwrap_int(list.get(ys, i))),
  )
end fn

use std.list

pub fn wrap(text: Str, width: Int) -> List[Str]
  var lines: List[Str] = []
  var current = ""
  for word in str.words(text)
    if current == ""
      set current = word
    else if str.len(current) + 1 + str.len(word) <= width
      set current = current + " " + word
    else
      set lines = list.push(lines, current)
      set current = word
    end if
  end for
  if current != ""
    set lines = list.push(lines, current)
  end if
  lines
end fn

`edges` describe a directed graph with non-negative costs. Return the cost of the
cheapest path from `from` to `to`, `Some(0)` when they are the same node, and
`None` when `to` is unreachable (or a node does not appear at all). The graph can
have thousands of edges: the solution must be much faster than trying every path.

Call it with named arguments, as Veld requires for three or more parameters:
`shortest(edges, from: "a", to: "b")`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.map

pub record Edge
  from: Str
  to: Str
  cost: Int
end record

fn adjacency(edges: List[Edge]) -> Map[Str, List[Edge]]
  var out: Map[Str, List[Edge]] = {}
  for e in edges
    set out = map.update(out, key: e.from, default: [], f: fn(es) => list.push(es, e))
  end for
  out
end fn

pub fn shortest(edges: List[Edge], from: Str, to: Str) -> Option[Int]
  let graph = adjacency(edges)
  var dist: Map[Str, Int] = {from: 0}
  var done: Map[Str, Bool] = {}
  while true
    var best: Option[Str] = None
    var best_cost = 0
    for node in map.keys(dist)
      if not map.has(done, node)
        let d = map.get_or(dist, key: node, default: 0)
        match best
          case None
            set best = Some(node)
            set best_cost = d
          case Some(_)
            if d < best_cost
              set best = Some(node)
              set best_cost = d
            end if
        end match
      end if
    end for
    match best
      case None => break
      case Some(node)
        set done = map.put(done, key: node, value: true)
        for e in map.get_or(graph, key: node, default: [])
          let candidate = best_cost + e.cost
          match map.get(dist, e.to)
            case Some(existing)
              if candidate < existing
                set dist = map.put(dist, key: e.to, value: candidate)
              end if
            case None => set dist = map.put(dist, key: e.to, value: candidate)
          end match
        end for
    end match
  end while
  map.get(dist, to)
end fn

Rules for `apply`: amounts must be positive (`Err("invalid amount")`); an unknown
account is `Err("unknown account: <id>")` (for a transfer check `from` first, then
`to`); a withdrawal or transfer that would make a balance negative is
`Err("insufficient funds")`; a transfer to the same account is `Err("same account")`.
On error the input is unchanged. `apply_all` applies the transactions in order and
stops at the first error, returning it.
reference:
use std.list
use std.map

pub record Account
  id: Str
  balance: Int
end record

pub type Tx
  case Deposit(id: Str, amount: Int)
  case Withdraw(id: Str, amount: Int)
  case Transfer(from: Str, to: Str, amount: Int)
end type

fn find(accounts: Map[Str, Account], id: Str) -> Result[Account, Str]
  match map.get(accounts, id)
    case Some(a) => Ok(a)
    case None => Err("unknown account: ${id}")
  end match
end fn

fn adjust(accounts: Map[Str, Account], account: Account, delta: Int) -> Result[Map[Str, Account], Str]
  let balance = account.balance + delta
  if balance < 0
    return Err("insufficient funds")
  end if
  Ok(map.put(accounts, key: account.id, value: Account{..account, balance: balance}))
end fn

pub fn apply(accounts: Map[Str, Account], tx: Tx) -> Result[Map[Str, Account], Str]
  match tx
    case Deposit(id, amount)
      if amount <= 0
        return Err("invalid amount")
      end if
      let account = find(accounts, id)?
      adjust(accounts, account: account, delta: amount)
    case Withdraw(id, amount)
      if amount <= 0
        return Err("invalid amount")
      end if
      let account = find(accounts, id)?
      adjust(accounts, account: account, delta: 0 - amount)
    case Transfer(from, to, amount)
      if amount <= 0
        return Err("invalid amount")
      end if
      let source = find(accounts, from)?
      let target = find(accounts, to)?
      if from == to
        return Err("same account")
      end if
      let after_debit = adjust(accounts, account: source, delta: 0 - amount)?
      adjust(after_debit, account: target, delta: amount)
  end match
end fn

pub fn apply_all(accounts: Map[Str, Account], txs: List[Tx]) -> Result[Map[Str, Account], Str]
  var current = accounts
  for tx in txs
    set current = apply(current, tx)?
  end for
  Ok(current)
end fn

`balanced` is true when every `(`, `[` and `{` in `text` is closed by the matching
bracket in the right order; all other characters are ignored. `first_error` returns

reference:
use std.list
use std.str

record Open
  symbol: Str
  index: Int
end record

fn partner(closer: Str) -> Str
  match closer
    case ")" => "("
    case "]" => "["
    case "}" => "{"
    case _ => ""
  end match
end fn

pub fn first_error(text: Str) -> Option[Int]
  var stack: List[Open] = []
  var i = 0
  for c in str.chars(text)
    if c == "(" or c == "[" or c == "{"
      set stack = list.push(stack, Open{symbol: c, index: i})
    else if c == ")" or c == "]" or c == "}"
      match list.last(stack)
        case Some(top)
          if top.symbol == partner(c)
            set stack = list.take(stack, list.len(stack) - 1)
          else
            return Some(i)
          end if
        case None => return Some(i)
      end match
    end if
    set i = i + 1
  end for
  match list.first(stack)
    case Some(o) => Some(o.index)
    case None => None
  end match
end fn

pub fn balanced(text: Str) -> Bool
  first_error(text) == None
end fn

    pub record Interval
      start: Int
      stop: Int
    end record

    pub fn merge(intervals: List[Interval]) -> List[Interval]

An interval covers `start` up to but not including `stop` (`start <= stop`; an
empty interval has `start == stop`). `merge` returns the smallest list of disjoint,

number of integer points covered by the union.
reference:
use std.list

pub record Interval
  start: Int
  stop: Int
end record

pub fn merge(intervals: List[Interval]) -> List[Interval]
  let sorted = list.sort_by(list.filter(intervals, fn(i) => i.stop > i.start), fn(i) => i.start)
  var out: List[Interval] = []
  for next in sorted
    match list.last(out)
      case Some(last)
        if next.start <= last.stop
          set out = list.set_at(
            out,
            index: list.len(out) - 1,
            item: Interval{start: last.start, stop: max_int(last.stop, next.stop)},
          )
        else
          set out = list.push(out, next)
        end if
      case None => set out = list.push(out, next)
    end match
  end for
  out
end fn

fn max_int(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  if a > b
    a
  else
    b
  end if
end fn

pub fn total_length(intervals: List[Interval]) -> Int
  list.sum(list.map(merge(intervals), fn(i) => i.stop - i.start))
end fn

    pub fn encode(text: Str) -> Str
    pub fn decode(text: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]

Run-length encoding of characters: `encode("aaabcc")` is `"3a1b2c"` (every run is
written as its length followed by the character; `""` encodes to `""`). Characters
are Unicode characters, not bytes. `decode` inverts `encode`: a count of one or
more digits followed by exactly one character, repeated. Malformed input (a
count without a character, a character without a count, or a count of `0`)
returns `Err("malformed input")`. `decode("")` is `Ok("")`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.str

pub fn encode(text: Str) -> Str
  var parts: List[Str] = []
  var current = ""
  var count = 0
  for c in str.chars(text)
    if c == current
      set count = count + 1
    else
      if count > 0
        set parts = list.push(parts, "${count}${current}")
      end if
      set current = c
      set count = 1
    end if
  end for
  if count > 0
    set parts = list.push(parts, "${count}${current}")
  end if
  str.join(parts, "")
end fn

pub fn decode(text: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
  var out: List[Str] = []
  var digits = ""
  for c in str.chars(text)
    if str.is_digit(c)
      set digits = digits + c
    else
      match str.to_int(digits)
        case Some(n)
          if n > 0
            set out = list.push(out, str.repeat(c, n))
            set digits = ""
          else
            return Err("malformed input")
          end if
        case None => return Err("malformed input")
      end match
    end if
  end for
  if digits != ""
    return Err("malformed input")
  end if
  Ok(str.join(out, ""))
end fn

Write `solution.veld` implementing a binary search tree of Ints:

    pub type Tree
      case Leaf
      case Node(left: Tree, value: Int, right: Tree)
    end type

    pub fn insert(tree: Tree, value: Int) -> Tree

`insert` keeps the tree ordered and ignores duplicates. `to_list` returns the

reference:
use std.list

pub type Tree
  case Leaf
  case Node(left: Tree, value: Int, right: Tree)
end type

pub fn insert(tree: Tree, value: Int) -> Tree
  match tree
    case Leaf => Node(left: Leaf, value: value, right: Leaf)
    case Node(left, v, right)
      if value < v
        Node(left: insert(left, value), value: v, right: right)
      else if value > v
        Node(left: left, value: v, right: insert(right, value))
      else
        tree
      end if
  end match
end fn

pub fn contains(tree: Tree, value: Int) -> Bool
  match tree
    case Leaf => false
    case Node(left, v, right)
      if value == v
        true
      else if value < v
        contains(left, value)
      else
        contains(right, value)
      end if
  end match
end fn

pub fn to_list(tree: Tree) -> List[Int]
  match tree
    case Leaf => []
    case Node(left, v, right) => to_list(left) + [v] + to_list(right)
  end match
end fn

pub fn height(tree: Tree) -> Int
  match tree
    case Leaf => 0
    case Node(left, _, right)
      let l = height(left)
      let r = height(right)
      1 + if l > r
        l
      else
        r
      end if
  end match
end fn

pub fn from_list(values: List[Int]) -> Tree
  list.fold(values, init: Leaf, step: insert)
end fn

Write `solution.veld` with

    pub record Sale
      region: Str
      product: Str
      units: Int
      price: Float
    end record

    pub fn report(sales: List[Sale]) -> List[Str]

Produce a text report: one line per region, sorted by region name, formatted

    <region>: <total units> units, revenue <revenue with 2 decimals>, top: <product>

where revenue is the sum of `units * price` over the region's sales, and `top` is
the product with the most units in that region (the alphabetically first one on a
tie). Empty input gives `[]`.
reference:
use std.list
use std.map
use std.math
use std.str

pub record Sale
  region: Str
  product: Str
  units: Int
  price: Float
end record

fn top_product(sales: List[Sale]) -> Str
  var units: Map[Str, Int] = {}
  for s in sales
    set units = map.update(units, key: s.product, default: 0, f: fn(n) => n + s.units)
  end for
  let ranked = list.sort_by(list.sort(map.keys(units)), fn(p) => 0 - map.get_or(units, key: p, default: 0))
  list.get_or(ranked, index: 0, fallback: "")
end fn

pub fn report(sales: List[Sale]) -> List[Str]
  let groups = list.group_by(sales, key: fn(s) => s.region)
  list.map(
    list.sort(map.keys(groups)),
    fn(region) => line(region, map.get_or(groups, key: region, default: [])),
  )
end fn

fn line(region: Str, sales: List[Sale]) -> Str
  let units = list.sum(list.map(sales, fn(s) => s.units))
  let revenue = list.sum_float(list.map(sales, fn(s) => math.to_float(s.units) * s.price))
  "${region}: ${units} units, revenue ${str.fixed(revenue, 2)}, top: ${top_product(sales)}"
end fn

Write `solution.veld` with

    pub fn days_between(from: Str, to: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
    pub fn add_days(date: Str, days: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]
    pub fn weekday_name(date: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]

Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings in UTC. `days_between` is the number of whole days
from `from` to `to` (negative if `to` is earlier). `add_days` returns the date that
many days later (or earlier for a negative count), formatted `YYYY-MM-DD`.
`weekday_name` is `Monday` ... `Sunday`. Any argument that is not a valid date gives
`Err("invalid date: <text>")` (check `from` before `to`). The standard library
module `std.datetime` helps; call `days_between(a, to: b)` with the second argument
named only if you use three or more parameters (here two is fine).
reference:
use std.datetime
use std.list
use std.str

fn parse(date: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
  match datetime.parse_iso(date + "T00:00:00Z")
    case Some(ms)
      if str.len(date) == 10
        Ok(ms)
      else
        Err("invalid date: ${date}")
      end if
    case None => Err("invalid date: ${date}")
  end match
end fn

fn day_ms() -> Int
  86400000
end fn

pub fn days_between(from: Str, to: Str) -> Result[Int, Str]
  let a = parse(from)?
  let b = parse(to)?
  Ok((b - a) / day_ms())
end fn

pub fn add_days(date: Str, days: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]
  let ms = parse(date)? + days * day_ms()
  Ok(str.slice(datetime.iso(ms), start: 0, stop: 10))
end fn

pub fn weekday_name(date: Str) -> Result[Str, Str]
  let ms = parse(date)?
  let names = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"]
  Ok(list.get_or(names, index: datetime.weekday(ms), fallback: "?"))
end fn

prompt:
Write `solution.veld` defining:

    pub record Renewal
      name: Str
      owner: Str
      category: Str
      expires_day: Int
    end record

    pub fn due(
      items: List[Renewal],
      today: Int,
      within: Int,
      owner: Str,
      category: Str,
    ) -> Result[List[Str], Str]

Return renewals whose `expires_day - today` is at most `within`, including
overdue renewals. An empty owner or category filter matches every value;
otherwise compare that field after trimming whitespace and ignoring case. Both
non-empty filters must match. A negative `within` returns
`Err("within must be zero or greater")`.

Sort results by `expires_day`, then by name on a tie. Format each line as:

    <status> | <name> | owner=<owner> | category=<category>

Status is `OVERDUE Nd`, `DUE TODAY`, or `DUE Nd`. Preserve the stored text in
the output; normalization is only for matching.
reference:
use std.list
use std.str

pub record Renewal
  name: Str
  owner: Str
  category: Str
  expires_day: Int
end record

fn normalized(value: Str) -> Str
  str.lower(str.trim(value))
end fn

fn matches(item: Renewal, owner: Str, category: Str) -> Bool
  let owner_matches = owner == "" or normalized(item.owner) == owner
  let category_matches = category == "" or normalized(item.category) == category
  owner_matches and category_matches
end fn

fn status(delta: Int) -> Str
  if delta < 0
    "OVERDUE ${-delta}d"
  else if delta == 0
    "DUE TODAY"
  else
    "DUE ${delta}d"
  end if
end fn

fn line(item: Renewal, today: Int) -> Str
  let delta = item.expires_day - today
  "${status(delta)} | ${item.name} | owner=${item.owner} | category=${item.category}"
end fn

pub fn due(items: List[Renewal], today: Int, within: Int, owner: Str, category: Str) -> Result[List[Str], Str]
  if within < 0
    return Err("within must be zero or greater")
  end if
  let owner_filter = normalized(owner)
  let category_filter = normalized(category)
  let filtered = list.filter(
    items,
    fn(item)
      let filters_match = matches(item, owner: owner_filter, category: category_filter)
      let window_matches = item.expires_day - today <= within
      filters_match and window_matches
    end fn,
  )
  let by_name = list.sort_by(filtered, key: fn(item) => item.name)
  let ordered = list.sort_by(by_name, key: fn(item) => item.expires_day)
  Ok(list.map(ordered, fn(item) => line(item, today)))
end fn
